evidence: Reviewed staged diff in MyAccessibilityService.kt: removed the named-close-node stage (findFirstNodeMatching for close/cerrar/dismiss/descartar with direct click and its own recycle path) from findAndClickCloseButton, so X detection now runs exclusively through the geometric stages - blank ImageView candidates within the popup subtree (findPopupContainer scope), top-40 percent band first, then full popup, then whole window, ranked by clickable-ness then rightmost then topmost; the geometric flow with its single recycle block remains intact; build.gradle.kts version bump to 0.3.45

aapt dump badging reports com.example.projectacc versionCode 60 versionName 0.3.45; compileDebugKotlin succeeded with no warnings; findFirstNodeMatching keeps its remaining caller findPopupContainer so no dead symbol remains

findings.claim: Deleting the named-node stage means an accessibility label containing close/cerrar/dismiss/descartar on a node other than the actual X would no longer receive the click, which was the reason the stage existed as a semantically safe first choice; the geometric ranking must now identify the button on its own. On the current popup the X is a blank ImageView in the top-right corner, so the band filter plus clickable-preferred rightmost ranking covers it, and the 300 ms post-click verification still catches a wrong pick by retrying up to three times; if a future popup layout marks the X with a label while making it non-clickable without a clickable parent, rank 0 candidates are still eligible and the rightmost-tiebreak decides.
proof_refs: findAndClickCloseButton now starts at the geometric comment with no findFirstNodeMatching call for close keywords
attemptNonCvClose still verifies closure after 300 ms and retries on CLICK_FAILED

findings.claim: The removed branch carried its own recycle sequence (named, scope, early return) while the geometric path recycles through the shared tail block (all minus rootNode/scope, then scope). With the branch gone there is a single exit path for recycling, which reduces the chance of double-recycle or leak; the candidates list can still contain scope itself when scope is a blank ImageView and the tail skips it via the scope reference check, so each node is recycled at most once.
proof_refs: the tail block recycles every candidate except rootNode and scope, then recycles scope when non-null, so each node is released once
no early return remains between candidate collection and the tail recycle block
